newsitem.title: USA: Poor visibility spurs Medaphis downgrade.
newsitem.headline: Poor visibility spurs Medaphis downgrade.

text.p: Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said on Wednesday its downgrade of Medaphis Corp's stock came because it lacked enough insight into what was happening at the medical information company.
In a report that cut Medaphis' rating to hold from buy, analyst Andrew Burns wrote, "We don't believe management has been as forthcoming as we Would like with operational issues.
"Consequently, we don't feel we have sufficient visibility on the company's fundamental performance to substantiate our buy rating."

Medaphis reported a third-quarter pro forma loss on Tuesday of $0.51 a share against a loss of $0.05 for the same period in 1995. The company's stock fell more than 30 percent in heavy trade on Tuesday and opened on Wednesday down 3/8 to a year's low of 10.
Burns lowered his fourth-quarter revenue estimate to $155 million from $165 million, and his estimate of earnings per share to a loss of $0.02 from a profit of $0.06.
For 1997, "we are lowering our revenue estimate to $750 million form $800 million, and our earnings per share estimate from $0.75 to $0.50."
